analysis:
The change is documentation only, in docs/developer/test.md. The visible head text (lines 921-1842) is a test guide, and the patch excerpt adds a new section, "Cluster service listeners after pairing again" (head lines 2465-2485, outside the supplied head_text units). No code, workflow, fixture or policy changes appear in the supplied units, so no threat-model control is weakened.

Security-relevant statements I checked in the visible text:
- The native serving qualification text (lines 944-992) describes owner-only 0700/0600 inputs, symlink refusal, an ephemeral SE signer, no persistent keys, no content, keys or proofs in observation.json, and an explicit statement that no deployment is qualified. This matches the TB-011/T-053/T-056 scope and over-claims nothing.
- The release and dev-branch lane description (lines 1314-1325) says Developer ID signing and notarization are enforced and nothing signs ad hoc. This is documentation of tests, not a change to any control.
- The SSD write-budget and cache test text (lines 1379-1386) retains the missing-volume, encryption, epoch, owner-only and no-fallback checks, consistent with T-041. There is no change to the TTL or the salt scoping.
- The diagnostics text keeps tokens, prompts and completions out of telemetry and heartbeats (lines 1578-1580).

The new pairing-change section in the patch only describes loopback-listener tests. It states that a re-pairing causes the earlier listeners to refuse the new pairing until restart, that a removed pairing stops both listeners, and that no production port is used. I could not verify the underlying implementation (ClusterService.Listening, the pairing store) because it is not supplied. If the listener-refresh behavior is a production change in another PR file, the next pass should check that stale listeners cannot authenticate with a revoked or earlier pairing key. That is an integration question, not a finding here.

No finding is raised.
